The TC-RAMS research team led by Professor Michael M. Bell is focused on improving our understanding and prediction of high-impact extreme weather

Colorado State University is a world leader in hurricane research and forecasting. Our group continues the long CSU tradition in hurricane forecasting with continually improving techniques for predicting tropical cyclone activity powered by cutting-edge new research.

Our team develops new software and AI tools that enable better data analysis and forecasts of high-impact weather. These tools include open source software for analyzing weather lidar and radar data, and AI products for better forecasts of hurricanes.

We collect data in field experiments to better study the atmosphere around the world. We manage and deploy the CSU SEA-POL radar, an NSF Community Facility, along with other weather radars on land, ships, aircraft, and satellites to study clouds and precipitation.
Our research team uses a combination of theoretical and numerical models to improve our understanding and prediction of extreme weather.
The primary targets of our research are on high-impact tropical weather, including hurricanes, heavy rain, and El Nino impacts.

column6: The TC-RAMS group welcomes visiting scientist Chun-Min Hsiao from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration

Chun-Min is a visiting researcher from Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA), where she works in the Typhoon and Severe Weather Forecast Division of the Weather Forecast Center. She develops forecast products and tools for CWA forecasters, such as the Deep Learning for Tropical Cyclones (DLTC) system, which she led into operations. The DLTC estimates and forecasts tropical cyclone intensity and wind structure from satellite imagery every hour. During typhoon warnings Chun-Min works forecast shifts, producing township-scale wind forecasts. Chun-Min earned her B.S. and M.S. in Atmospheric Sciences from National Taiwan University, where she applied deep learning to satellite observations of tropical cyclones. During her visit to CSU’s Atmospheric Science Department, Chun-Min is working on rapid intensification guidance for CWA. In her spare time, she enjoys cooking, hiking, and spending time with her family and her cat.
